pamphlet_excerpts: A properly working plumbing system protects: Plumbing systems carry water into and out of a home through a system of pipes (p. 20).

A properly working plumbing system protects Principle 2: For the health and safety of the people wholive there, the water entering the home through the water-supplysystem must be pure and clean (p. 20).
A properly working plumbing system protects Principle 3: Wastewater should never come into contact with the water that the family uses for drinking, bathing, or washing clothes anddishes (p. 20).

A properly working plumbing system protects Principle 4: This is the main reason that it is essential that your family's plumbing system be properly installed and regularlychecked to make sure it is in good (p. 20).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (A properly working plumbing system protects): Plumbing regulations have been developed to help make sure that plumbing is installed and maintained correctly (p. 20).
Step 2 (A properly working plumbing system protects): Theseregulations, commonly called plumbing codes, are important inpreventing the water-supply system from becoming contaminated (p. 20).
Step 3 (A properly working plumbing system protects): National plumbing codes exist that give specific regulations for all plumbingoperations (p. 20).
Step 4 (A properly working plumbing system protects): Many communities have adopted these regulationsor amended them to fit their local needs (p. 20).

pamphlet_excerpts: Drawing and Explain How A: Make A Drawing: The air vents are an importantpart of waste disposal, which is why the drainage system isoften called the drain-waste-vent (DWV) system (p. 9).
Drawing and Explain How A Principle 2: Make A Drawing Principle 2: The drain andvent pipes are tied together, or share pipes, and use the sametypes of pipe (p. 9).
Drawing and Explain How A Principle 3: Make A Drawing Principle 3: As you can see in the illustration showing the drainage and supply system, the main vent is an extension of the soilpipe (p. 9).
Drawing and Explain How A Principle 4: Make A Drawing Principle 4: Without air vents, the plumbing system would becomeair-bound, like a small-necked bottle filled with water (p. 9).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Drawing and Explain How A): Step 1 (Make A Drawing): The plumbing system of a house relies on two basic things: pressure and gravity (p. 9).
Step 2 (Drawing and Explain How A): Step 2 (Make A Drawing): When you turn on a faucet, you can feel the water pressure, weak or strong (p. 9).

Step 3 (Drawing and Explain How A): Step 3 (Make A Drawing): The pressure comes from a pump (if the water comes from a well) or from gravity (if the water comes from a water tower or reservoir) (p. 9).
Step 4 (Drawing and Explain How A): Step 4 (Make A Drawing): When you flush a toilet or pull the plug from a bathtub, gravity pulls the waste and water down and away from the house (p. 9).

pamphlet_excerpts: Careers & Professional Pathways: Plumbing, including pipe fitting, is an important and well-paidoccupation (p. 8).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 2: It covers installations and repairs in homes, commercial properties, and factories (p. 8).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 3: Plumbing pipelines are used for water supply, waste drainage, natural-gas heating, and many other purposes (p. 8).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 4: As a Scout, your major interest in plumbing probably will be in the field of home repairs (p. 8).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Careers & Professional Pathways): If a faucet leaks, a pipe freezes, or a plumbing fixture does not operate properly, you will want to know how to evaluate the problem (p. 8).
